title: AES-256: Dual-result xtime: key recovery (Blömer–Seifert, FC2003)

target.description: Complete AES-256 master key using the Dual-result xtime feedback model; the longer-key completion is a qualitative extension with no total data budget.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Arbitrary key of the stated AES instance in an implementation meeting the fault and feedback assumptions.
setting.plaintext_model: For a target first-round key byte, use chosen values i=0,...,N-1 in its plaintext byte; other bytes are arbitrary/random. Whole-key extension repeats for the required key material, with adaptive inputs for long keys.

fault_model.target: The xtime[0] temporary of a dual-result implementation, after both alternatives are computed and before xtime[f] is selected.
fault_model.granularity: Arbitrary incorrect value in one specific temporary result byte.
fault_model.timing: During first-round MixColumns, before result selection; long-key extension also requires observing later key additions through the following round.
fault_model.location: Precisely the xtime[0] computation associated with the targeted S-box output byte.
fault_model.value_control: Enforce xtime[0]' != xtime[0]; no particular error value is needed.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Each attempted injection yields a correct/incorrect outcome. Ciphertext-comparison feedback additionally needs a correct reference for the same input, outside the stated attempt count.
fault_model.feedback: Observable correct-versus-incorrect encryption outcome. Section1 permits alternatives: a device reset/error flag; comparison with a fault-free ciphertext; or detectable recomputation timing. Only the binary outcome is required, not the faulty ciphertext bytes. An incorrect output means the saved MSB was0; a correct output means the corrupted xtime[0] branch was discarded because MSB=1.

assumptions: Successful localization and the stipulated fault-value effect are model assumptions, not measured acquisition success rates.
The ciphertext-validity alternatives are interchangeable only as a binary observation; the source does not cost each feedback channel's calibration or reference executions separately.
Recovery target: Complete AES-256 master key using the Dual-result xtime feedback model; the longer-key completion is a qualitative extension with no total data budget.

The implementation must expose precisely the specified temporary, instruction, RAM input or register-bank location. A timing-resistant xtime implementation alone does not establish these fault controls.

Section5.1 refers to the Section4 smaller-block/longer-key extension. Additional adaptive first-round-state control and later-round feedback are required; no full parameterized acquisition budget is given.

time.note: No numerical complete-attack offline runtime is reported.

data.reported: Qualitative longer-key extension; total attempt count not reported
data.note: Section5.1 points to the Section4 extension but does not tabulate a complete long-key budget. No384/512 extrapolation is inserted.

memory.reported: Prediction table T has256 × N Boolean entries; peak memory not reported
memory.note: This is the table's logical shape, not a numerical peak-memory or byte-storage claim.

preprocessing.note: The source specifies this reusable table but gives no preprocessing-time measurement or normalized operation count.

success.description: No numerical recovery success is given for this endpoint at its recorded budget. The complete-key extension uses the approximate16-observations-per-byte reasoning or a qualitative longer-key extension, not the N=256 per-byte endpoint. The source N=256 guarantee is not transferred to this approximate budget. AES192/256 additionally require adaptive later-round observations; their whole-key budget and joint success remain unquantified. The local exact-MSB relation assumes the stated physical effect and reliable binary feedback; no acquisition yield or independence is invented.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Theoretical deterministic guarantees require the stated ideal model; local filters, characteristic products, expected counts and physical acquisition are separate. Costs, targets, settings, existing conflicts and full-audit gates are unchanged.

components.description: Sections5.1–5.5: provided the specified fault effect/location and reliable correctness feedback, the target S-box output MSB is determined exactly. The dual-result corruption causes an incorrect output iff MSB0; the corrupted alternative is discarded when MSB1. This local observation is not physical fault acquisition or whole-key success.
